Privacy

Last updated 10 November 2026

Krunk is a browser that keeps out of your business. This page says what the Krunk website and the optional Krunk account hold about you, for how long, and who else is involved.

Without an account

  • The browser sends no telemetry. It contacts this site once a day to check for an update, sending only its version, and fetches filter lists for the ad blocker.
  • The optional AI agent (off by default) sends what you ask it to work on (your messages and the page content it reads) directly from your PC to the AI provider you set up with your own key. We don't receive it, and that provider's own privacy terms apply. Passwords, payment cards and your API key are never sent.
  • This website sets no cookies, has no analytics, and our server keeps no access log.

With an account

An account is optional. It is needed only for sync between your devices.

  • Your email address, to sign in and to send you account emails (confirmation, password reset, security notices). No newsletters, no tracking pixels.
  • Your password, stored only as a salted, slow hash (Argon2id). We can't read it.
  • Two-step verification, if you turn it on: the authenticator secret, encrypted, and the backup codes as hashes.
  • Sign-in sessions: when they started and were last used, the browser's user-agent string, the IP address and the country it came from. A session cookie keeps you signed in to this website (up to 7 days; 12 hours idle).
  • Security events (registration, sign-in, password and two-step changes, devices added and removed, data downloads, sync resets) with IP address and country; see below.
  • An email log: which kind of account email we sent you (for example "new device") and when. Not the message itself.

Activity & IP addresses

Your account page shows you the activity of the last 90 days: each sign-in and security change, when it happened, the full IP address and country it came from, and which device or browser it was. Devices and signed-in browsers show their last IP address too. Only you see this, when signed in; it is your own data. After 90 days the entries and their IP addresses are deleted.

Adding a device by QR code

"Add a device" on your account page shows a QR code that works once, for 5 minutes. When a phone scans it, we keep what you need to decide whether it is yours: the phone's IP address and country, the device name or browser it reports, and when it asked. You approve or deny it on your signed-in screen. The code and these details are deleted at the latest about 70 minutes after the code expires (an hourly clean-up); an approved device is then listed like any other. The scan itself shows in your activity, with its IP address, like any other event.

Synced data

With sync on (optional, since Krunk 0.9.0), your bookmarks, history, open tabs, settings and passwords are encrypted on your devices before they are uploaded, with keys only your devices hold. Our server stores ciphertext it can't read. It does see how much you store, when your devices sync, and which devices are linked. The Krunk website never asks for your sync passphrase or recovery key.

Resetting sync on your account page deletes all your encrypted sync data and the sync keys we store, at once. Your devices stay signed in and keep what they hold locally; the next one that turns sync on sets it up again.

Downloading your data

"Download all your data" on your account page gives you one JSON file with everything we hold about your account: the account itself, devices, signed-in browsers, activity with IP addresses, pending device links and QR codes, the email log, and your synced records encrypted exactly as stored. It contains no keys, so the synced records stay unreadable without your devices. The file is only downloaded in your browser; it is never emailed.

How long we keep it

  • IP addresses and activity are removed after 90 days. Countries stay while the session exists.
  • The email log is kept for 90 days.
  • QR codes for adding a device and what a phone sent with them are deleted within about 70 minutes after the code expires.
  • Ended sign-in sessions are deleted after 30 days.
  • Accounts never confirmed are deleted after 7 days.
  • Your account is kept until you delete it; unused accounts are not deleted automatically.
  • Backups of the database are kept for 14 days.

Deleting your account

Delete your account yourself on the account page ("Delete account…"): it asks for your password (and your two-step code, if it is on) and your email address typed out. Deletion removes the account and everything attached to it from our database at once: devices, sessions, activity, the email log and all synced data and keys. We send one receipt to your address. Download your data first if you want a copy.

Backups still hold the account until they expire, within 14 days. To make sure a restore can't bring it back, we keep a deletion log with only the deleted account's internal id and the time: 30 days in the database and 45 days in a copy beside the backups. A restore deletes every account in that log again.

Who else is involved

  • Cloudflare delivers this site. It handles every connection, so it sees your IP address and the pages you request, under its own privacy policy. The account forms use Cloudflare Turnstile to keep bots out; it runs a check in your browser and doesn't use cookies to track you.
  • Our email provider delivers the account emails, so it handles your email address and the message.

We don't sell or share your data with anyone else, and we show no ads.

Contact

Questions, or help with a copy of your data or deletion: privacy@209.wf.
